title: Prefill/Decode congestion controller with kernel-aware demux and latency-cost SLAs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a congestion controller for the prefill->decode pipeline that dynamically demultiplexes and shapes requests based on kernel probe signals, attention sparsity estimates, and tenant latency-cost SLAs. The controller should reduce tail latency under load while improving GPU token efficiency and preventing kernel saturation during mixed workloads.
background: We observe recurring tail latency spikes when bursts of long-context prefill requests coincide with decode-heavy streams. Existing phase splitters allocate static quotas or simple priority lanes which either starve decode or waste headroom. Kernel selection (FP16 vs int8 kernels, sparse-attn fast-paths) can change per-request throughput; without a congestion controller the runtime oscillates between suboptimal kernel choices and high queuing overhead.
goals: 1) Maintain tenant p95 decode latency within SLA for latency-focused tiers during 95th-percentile bursts. 2) Recover GPU utilization lost to over-conservative static isolation by opportunistic demuxing. 3) Use kernel probing signals to steer requests toward compatible kernels without violating SLAs.
non_goals: Do not change model quantization defaults in this ticket. This is not a replacement for long-term admission control (rate limiting at API gateway); focus is intra-GPU runtime arbitration.
design_overview: The controller is a lightweight runtime component that sits between prefill and decode stages. It maintains per-tenant soft deadines and absolute hard-deadlines and exposes a leaky-bucket shaped token queue. Incoming prefill requests are classified by: estimated decode token count, attention sparsity hint, kernel affinity (from kernel-probe heuristic), and tenant SLA tier. A demultiplexer places requests into dynamic lanes: latency-lane (low headroom), throughput-lane (opportunistic batch), and probe-lane (small probed items for kernel validation). Allocation proportions adapt with a short moving window using a congestion signal derived from kernel queue depth and per-GPU pipeline occupancy.
kernel_signals: 1) kernel_probe_latency: recent median latency for a small probe batch on candidate kernel. 2) kernel_utilization: percent occupancy reported by kernel telemetry. 3) attention_sparsity_hint: scalar [0..1] from tokenizer/analysis indicating expected sparsity. 4) kv_cache_size_hint: expected decode KV cache growth. These signals are used to compute a kernel_affinity score to prefer kernels that reduce tail latency per-request.
scheduler_policy:
- Soft deadlines: each request has soft_deadline = now + tenant_sla_margin. Soft deadline misses trigger lane promotion.
- Hard deadlines: if queueing would violate hard_deadline, request is hedged (spawn decode on fallback kernel) or preempted.
- Demuxing: small requests (< X tokens) are shunted to probe/fast batch lane. Large prefills with high sparsity go to throughput lane.
- Backpressure: if kernel_utilization > util_high_thresh and kernel_probe_latency trending up, reduce throughput_lane admission and increase latency_lane capacity.
- Opportunistic kernel selection: prefer int8/quant kernels for throughput lane if kernel_probe_latency within tolerance and attention_sparsity_hint low.
- Fairness: proportional tenant weights with minimal guaranteed slots for latency tier; soft rebalancing every 200ms.
metrics: Primary: tenant_p50_decode_latency, tenant_p95_decode_latency, tenant_p99_decode_latency, tail_decode_hedge_rate. Secondary: gpu_kernel_utilization, tokens_per_sec_per_gpu, kernel_probe_success_rate, queued_requests_by_lane, prefill_to_decode_handshake_time.
acceptance_criteria: Under synthetic mixed workload (50% long-prefill, 50% short-decode bursts) maintain p95 decode latency for latency-tier tenants within SLA (baseline SLA = 120ms) and reduce p99 by at least 15% vs current baseline.
GPU token throughput (tokens/sec) improves or stays within 5% of baseline while p95 targets met.
No regression in correctness: kernel_probe must not alter outputs beyond existing approved kernel variants.
Automated canary rollout with circuit breaker: if p99 increases >30% during rollout, automatically rollback to previous scheduler config.
Add dashboards and alerting for queued_requests_by_lane > threshold, kernel_probe_failure_rate > 2%.
Unit and e2e tests for lane assignment logic, soft/hard deadline enforcement, and kernel affinity scoring.

implementation_notes: Controller should be lock-free style; prefer simple atomic counters over global locks to avoid slowing hot path.
Start with conservative default: latency-lane=40%, throughput-lane=50%, probe-lane=10%, then enable adaptive adjustments after canary.
Hedging must be rate-limited to avoid doubling GPU work; cap hedged requests to 5% of throughput.
Expose tuning knobs via runtime config and keep per-cluster safe defaults.
Use existing kernel-probe infra (ENG-523411) to avoid duplicating telemetry plumbing.
Ensure controller respects tenant isolation policies and does not allow cross-tenant metric leakage.
testing_plan: Unit: lane decision FSM with mocked kernel signals.
Integration: run mixed-workload harness across a 4-GPU node and compare p95/p99 to baseline.
Chaos: kill kernel probe responses and validate graceful fallback to probe failure path.
A/B: 10% traffic canary for 48 hours, compare customer impact metrics and GPU utilization.
Benchmark: stress test with 10x burst factor to validate hard deadline enforcement without hanging the pipeline.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal lab tests with synthetic traffic (complete)
Stage 1: Canary - 5% of production tenants, latency-tier excluded from initial canary unless opt-in (48h)
Stage 2: Expand to 25% with autoscaling profile tuned, monitor for regressions (72h)
Stage 3: Full rollout with gradual ramp and observation window (7 days), postmortem and tuning after ramp.
Rollback triggers: p99 regress >30%, kernel_probe_failure_rate >2%, CPU/GPU overload >90% sustained for 5m.
open_questions: What is the safe default threshold for attention_sparsity_hint to prefer sparse-attn kernels? (proposal: 0.6)
Should we expose per-tenant hard_deadline overrides? (security/ops implication)
How to metricize cost-per-token impact of hedging accurately across shared GPUs?
Is 200ms rebalancing window sufficiently responsive for microbursts? Run sim to validate.
